cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: What Really Happened?
cards.instruction: Find the truth by comparing details, repeating questions, and testing which parts of the story remain consistent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For the parcel you handed the driver, you've written 'bag' and 'box'. Describe the packaging, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It had handles. That's why I said bag.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Handles don't settle it. What were they attached to?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A cardboard box. I put it inside a shopping bag, then took it out at the van.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two containers. Start again at the van, please. Which one actually left your hands?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 requests a packaging description instead of labels. A3 corrects B2's handles-equals-bag inference, and A5 uses B4's two-container account to repeat the precise handover test.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 explains the bag label through handles; A3 tests attachment; B4 supplies nesting and removal; A5 retests the van moment rather than assuming which container was handed over.

relationship.evidence: B2/B4 are plausible recollections offered by someone trying to describe packaging, not deliberate evasions needed for a punchline.

heightening.evidence: B4 reconciles the contradictory labels but opens a handover uncertainty; A5 insists on the exact action rather than declaring the form solved.

specificity.evidence: A1 identifies a parcel handed to a driver and written conflicting labels. B4 locates the unpacking at the van, establishing A5's repeated scene.
